title: JobStatus
description:
The `GET /v1/jobs/:id` body (blackwall-serve `JobStatusResponse`), reduced
to the documented contract surface. Unknown fields are ignored (additive
rule); `run_hash` is present **iff** `state=done`.

action_id.description:
The reflex action id serve received on dispatch, verbatim (CER-2276
§6). Follows `base_commit`: `#[serde(default)]` and ALWAYS serialized —
`null` when the dispatch carried none; a missing key means a serve that
predates the field. Do not add `skip_serializing_if`.

base_commit.description:
The commit the run's jail was cut from (EST-251 pin; read route from
soma#410). Mirrors serve's field exactly: `#[serde(default)]` and
ALWAYS serialized — `null` means the run recorded no base (pre-EST-251
job, or a working tree that is not a git repo); a MISSING key means a
serve that predates the field. Do not add `skip_serializing_if`; the two
must stay distinguishable.

changeset.description: The run's changeset hash, if the executor produced one.

containment.description:
What serve OBSERVED it enforced for this run (EST-318). Executor-
attested, by value; absent when no containment was requested.

containment_attestation.description:
The JSON text of a [`crate::attestation::SignedContainmentAttestation`]
(§5). Always serialized; `null` until serve signs. reflex seals only
from this, never from the unsigned `containment` above.

escapement_attempt.description:
escapement's 0-based attempt counter serve received, verbatim (§6).
Same always-serialized rule as `action_id`.

run_hash.description: blackwall's content-addressed run hash — the durable custody pointer.

terminal.description:
Terminal classification (`"Completed"`/`"Crashed"`/`"Error"`), present
once the job reaches a terminal state.

A string on the wire, not a tagged enum: blackwall-serve Debug-formats
its internal `McpTerminal` (`format!("{t:?}")`), so these spellings are
variant names, not serde renames. Modeled as `String` here — a closed
enum would turn a blackwall-side variant addition into a reflex-side
parse failure, which the contract's unknown-tolerance forbids.

world.description: The world commit linking parent → child tree.

AppliedContainment.description:
What the executor OBSERVED it enforced for one run.

Executor-attested. A reader records it as attested by the executor, never
as verified by the reader.

profile_digest.description:
The digest of the profile the executor resolved. Must equal the
request's [`Containment::profile_digest`]; a difference means the
registry changed and the executor should have refused.

EnforcedLayer.description: One layer the executor observed in force.

evidence.description:
The observation BY VALUE: a compact JSON extract of what was read (a
jail probe result, the CiliumEndpoint policy status, the guest and
host kernel identities), carried as JSON text so it is byte-stable in
the record. Never a label, a stamp, or a reference to an object that
may be garbage-collected before anyone audits it. Empty is no evidence.

layer.description:
`"landlock"`, `"landlock-exec"`, `"kata"`, `"cnp"`, `"tetragon"` — an
open set; the requirement is whatever the profile's `required_layers`
names.

JobState.description:
A job's lifecycle state (`GET /v1/jobs/:id`).

`Unknown` absorbs states this build has never heard of (`#[serde(other)]`):
the contract's posture is that an unknown state is *not yet terminal* —
guessing wrong seals a false outcome permanently, waiting merely costs
another poll.
